result:
I would make no file changes and run no commands before asking.

The review finding conflicts with the plan's own text, so it is my partner's decision. Task 4 of the plan requires `format_time(1510) == '01:10:00'` and an hour "taken modulo 24". Spec section 3 requires `25:10:00` and says an hour must never wrap inside one trip. A fix subagent would have to contradict the plan, and I shouldn't dispatch that without a ruling. I also shouldn't dismiss the finding because the plan mandates the behavior. The implementer built what the plan said, so nothing is wrong with its work.

**Message to my partner:**

> Task 4 (`format_time`, commit 7c1d9e0) passed the plan's own steps, but the review found a conflict between the plan and the spec. I need a ruling before dispatching a fix.
>
> - **Plan, Task 4:** `format_time(1510) == '01:10:00'`, with the hour taken modulo 24.
> - **Spec section 3 (`specs/ferry-feed-export.md`):** a stop at 01:10 the next morning is written `25:10:00`. Planners sort stops by this string, so the hour must not wrap to 00-23 inside one trip.
> - **Review (Important):** the modulo-24 behavior sorts a trip's late stops before its early ones.
>
> **My recommendation:** the spec governs. Drop the modulo and make the hour keep counting, so `format_time(1510) == '25:10:00'`, with `format_time(540) == '09:00:00'` unchanged. This needs a change to the plan's Task 4 test and its Step 2 wording, as well as the code.
>
> If you agree, I'll resume the Task 4 implementer (fix round 1) with the finding and the corrected expectation. It will re-run `uv run pytest -q tests/test_times.py` and report the command and output. Then I'll dispatch a scoped re-review. If you'd rather keep modulo-24, tell me and I'll record that as a ruling and leave the code as is.
>
> Tasks 1-3 are complete in the ledger. I'm holding Task 4 and everything after it until you answer.
